title: A lead set on the work order page sends it to the bottom (release)
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • User {User-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dispatcher Two) has Work orders > View and Create & Edit at {Location-A} and is signed in in a second browser.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha), {Technician-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo) and {Technician-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Cal Charlie) are active staff members at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customers {Customer-A} to {Customer-E} are used by this case only, their names start with the same words (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Reassign Bottom") and end, in name order, with Aardvark Co, Abbey Co, Bravo Co, Delta Co and Echo Co.
  • Approved work orders: {Work-order-3} (for {Customer-C}) and {Work-order-4} (for {Customer-D}) are led by {Technician-B}; {Work-order-1} (for {Customer-A}), {Work-order-2} (for {Customer-B}) and {Work-order-5} (for {Customer-E}) are led by {Technician-C} (for example S10043-17721 to S10043-17725).
  • Nobody has reordered {Technician-B}'s work at {Location-A}, so {Technician-B}'s column starts in customer-name order: {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the shared start of the customer names (for example ZZAUTOTEST F3 Reassign Bottom) in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Open {Work-order-2}, pick {Technician-B} in Lead Technician on the work order page, then go back to Work Orders > All > Board View with the same search.
  5. Read the order of {Technician-B}'s column.
  6. Drag {Work-order-5}'s card from {Technician-C}'s column and drop it between {Work-order-3} and {Work-order-4} in {Technician-B}'s column.
  7. Click Tech View in the display switcher and read {Technician-B}'s group.
  8. In the second browser, as {User-B}, open Work Orders > All, type the same search, and read {Technician-B}'s work in Tech View and in Board View.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the Work Orders page shows the All tab.
  • Step 2: only this case's work orders show.
  • Step 3: Board View shows {Technician-B}'s column reading {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}. {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-5} are in {Technician-C}'s column.
  • Step 4: {Work-order-2}'s work order page shows Lead Technician {Technician-B}, and Board View shows again with the same search.
  • Step 5: {Technician-B}'s column reads {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}, {Work-order-2}. A lead set on the work order page goes to the bottom, even though by customer name it would come first.
  • Step 6: {Work-order-5} lands where it was dropped. {Technician-B}'s column reads {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-5}, {Work-order-4}, {Work-order-2}.
  • Step 7: Tech View shows the same order in {Technician-B}'s group.
  • Step 8: {User-B} sees the same order in both views.

Release copy of C97007 (in the Fast-follow folder). It leaves out giving a new lead from the lead technician dialog in the card's More actions menu, which waits on SV-11522 / SV-11524: Chris Ward (product owner) made these fast-follows for after the release (Slack, 20 Oct 2026, https://shopview.slack.com/archives/C0C41RV3T3L/p1792455057423139).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-R14 and S2-R6, read 19 Oct 2026. In version 53 (15 Oct 2026) S2-R6 was reworded to spell out the List's tie-break and to point to S9-R14; the expected results are unchanged. Starting order (customer name A to Z): Review Decisions page 853901313, DR-45 (29 Sep 2026). Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R14: “A work order that gets a new lead from the lead technician dialog (Assign or Reassign lead technician) or from its detail page goes to the bottom of the new technician’s work, for everyone at the location, in both views. A work order dragged to a technician goes where it is dropped. Removing the lead with the menu’s Unassign action (S11-R9) or on the detail page puts the work order in Unassigned in the initial sort, not at the bottom, so it is not lost behind every other unassigned work order. Going to the bottom applies only to work moved onto a technician. A work order created or split off with a lead keeps the initial sort (S9-R3).”
  • S2-R6: “Before a manual order is saved, use the List’s default work order sort, ties included, exactly as the List sorts today: work orders for the same customer go by start date, newest first. The List itself does not change. A work order that gets a new lead after it was created goes to the bottom of that technician’s work instead (S9-R14).”

AUTOMATION: READY
